conviction_note: abs_move 4.5 (ADR's own print reactions run -2.2% to -11.6%, realised vol 37.5%) times a p_up of 53: the only lean is that peers reporting after Wipro last spoke (TCS +0.5% cc bought +5.5%, HCLTech lifted its guide floor, Accenture beat and guided 3-6%) have raised the sector bar while Wipro's consensus is Strong Sell with a $1.70 target below spot; against that, the ADR has already run +7.2% in five sessions on exactly that read, the Meta cut lands on the Q3 guide, and this ADR line has sold most of its prints. Findings sum to +0.6; the scaled number is smaller because the sign is close to a coin flip.
bar: IT services revenue -0.5% to -1.4% QoQ cc (Jefferies -1.4, Nuvama -1.0, Emkay -1.0 USD, MOFSL -0.5, JM -0.5, PL -0.5), EBIT margin +40bp to ~16.4%, Q3 FY27 guide expected -2% to 0% cc (Emkay, Nuvama) or -1.5% to +0.5% (Jefferies); company guide for Q2 is $2,574-2,627M / -1.5% to +0.5% cc. Sources: https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/wipro-q2-fy27-results-preview/ (2026-10-14) and https://www.tradingview.com/news/moodys:ab25a0f6a0c64:0-wipro-q2-preview-brokerages-expect-weak-revenue-growth-margin-recovery/ (poll -0.5% to -1%), company guide https://www.wipro.com/content/dam/nexus/en/investor/quarterly-results/2026-2027/q1fy27/press-release-q1fy27.pdf (2026-07-16). Two agreeing estimate sources plus a company guide, so sizes are not capped.
positioning_check: ADR short interest 102,750,718 ADS at the 2026-09-30 settlement (published 2026-10-09), -0.84% vs 09-15, 14.2 days to cover on 11.0M average daily volume, 1.05% of float (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/WIT/short-interest). Option chain unusable: 615 contracts total OI, put/call OI 3.42, no two-sided ATM quote, so no skew is readable. Sell-side: 4 Sell / 0 Buy, consensus 'Strong Sell', target $1.70 vs spot $1.79-1.80 (JPMorgan Underweight $1.70 on 2026-06-24, CLSA Underperform 2026-08-19). ADR +7.19% over 5 sessions and +6.55% over 20, from a 52-week low of $1.59; NSE line Rs 162.25 (10-05) to Rs 170.35 (10-14, +1.35% on the day). The short is crowded by days-to-cover but trivial as a share of float; the sell-side bar is low.

findings.finding: Three peers reported after Wipro guided Q2 on 2026-07-16 and all three read better than Wipro's -1.5%/+0.5% cc guide implied: TCS (2026-10-09) grew +0.5% QoQ cc with BFSI +2.5% and UK +3.5%, North America +0.4%, and the stock rose 5.46%; HCLTech (2026-10-12) raised the floor of its FY27 cc guide to 2.5-4% from 1-4%; Accenture's quarter to Aug 31 (reported late Sep) printed +7% LC above the top of its own range and guided FY27 +3-6% LC with the stock up ~18-23%. Brokerage previews dated 10-14 still model Wipro at -0.5% to -1.4% cc and a Q3 guide of -2% to 0%, so the sector read has improved more than Wipro's bar has moved.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ADR has sold its own guide most times: -2.2% on 2026-04-16 when the Q1 guide was -2% to 0% (https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/stocks/story/wipro-adr-slips-over-2-after-q4-fy26-results-whats-driving-the-move-526034-2026-04-16); -11.6% on the Jul-2024 revenue miss (https://businessworld.in/article/wipro-stock-tumbles-8-as-revenue-declines-adr-ends-116-lower-526797); ADRs down 4-6% after the Jan-2025 print (https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/infosys-wipro-shares-in-focus-as-adrs-plunge-4-6-overnight-461110-2025-01-17). The NSE line rose +1.8% on the Q1 FY27 print despite a margin low. Peer prints in the sector were bought this quarter (TCS +5.5%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the ADR is +7.2% in five sessions and the NSE line +5% since 10-05 on the TCS/HCL prints. What is not in the price is the bar itself: every preview dated 10-14 still models a cc decline and a -2% to 0% Q3 guide, and the sell-side is 4 Sell / 0 Buy with a target below spot, so a guide of -1% to +1% or better would be a beat on the line the stock trades on. If it were priced, the previews would carry a flat-to-positive Q3 guide and at least one Hold.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a Wipro number. Independent sources point the same way: HCLTech guide raise https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/hcltech-net-profit-rises-21-to-5132-crore-in-q2-fy27-revenue-up-115 (2026-10-12); Accenture Q4 FY26 release https://newsroom.accenture.com/content/4q-full-fy26-earnings/accenture-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2026-results.pdf; TCS fact sheet https://www.tcs.com/content/dam/tcs/investor-relations/financial-statements/2026-27/q2/Presentations/Q2%202026-27%20Fact%20Sheet.pdf. Against it: Wipro's own Q1 call said the Americas (~60% of revenue) were soft and healthcare and E&U weak, and TCS's India revenue fell 10.3% QoQ.

findings.finding: Meta, a top-20 Wipro client, cut its outsourced IT work with Wipro by at least 25% (about $100M/yr to about $75M/yr), reported by Mint on 2026-08-02/03, three weeks AFTER Wipro set the Q2 guide; neither company has commented. $25M/yr is ~$6M a quarter, about 0.24% of IT services revenue, and lands on the Q3 FY27 guide rather than the reported Q2. Net of the rest of the company (13 large deals booked in Q1, $1.63B large-deal TCV, Mindsprint adding a full quarter) it is small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ADR fell 2.2% on the Q4 FY26 print when the forward guide read -2% to 0% (businesstoday 2026-04-16); a weak guide is the line this name has paid on.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small, so the Indian brokerage previews may already carry it; none of the 10-14 previews names Meta. If priced, the Q3 guide expectation would sit below the Q2 range rather than at the same -2% to 0%. Filed small because it is an unconfirmed press report and 0.24% of revenue.
findings.independence: Secondary coverage of one Mint report: https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/meta-cuts-wipro-outsourcing-by-25-million-to-75-million-annually/tldr and https://finviz.com/news/375787/meta-scales-back-wipro-outsourcing-following-ai-led-business-restructuring. The Estée Lauder item (Accenture added as a vendor, March 2026, Reuters) is merged here as context and is already inside the Q1 guide.

findings.finding: Wipro's acquisition of selected Alpha Net Consulting customer contracts (consideration up to $70.8M), twice guided to close by 2026-09-30, was pushed to 2026-12-31 in a filing on 2026-09-30/10-01; JM Financial's 10-14 preview still attributes ~40bp of revenue each to Mindsprint and AlphaNet, so any broker model that counted AlphaNet in Q2 is ~0.4% too high on reported revenue, while Mindsprint's full quarter (two months in Q1) is a real ~0.3-0.4% sequential add that is inside the company's own guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A reported-revenue miss against the LSEG estimate on 2026-07-16 (Rs 24,479 cr vs 24,776 cr) still saw the NSE line +1.8%; the ADR's -11.6% in Jul-2024 was a revenue miss. Mixed.
findings.why_not_priced: The delay is a filing nobody wrote a note on; the 10-14 preview that still counts an AlphaNet contribution is the evidence it is not in at least one broker's number. Inference about broker models, not a company number, so small.
findings.independence: The June filing with the $70.8M consideration and the original 09-30 target: https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/wipro-revises-timeline-for-alpha-net-contract-acquisition-targets-september-end-completion/article-195862/ (2026-06). The JM attribution is one line in the Kotak Neo preview (https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/wipro-q2-fy27-results-preview/), which does not say whether JM's Q2 estimate includes it.

findings.finding: Cross-currency and rupee against the guide's assumptions (GBP/USD 1.34, EUR/USD 1.16, USD/INR 94.50): the euro traded ~1.14-1.15 and sterling ~1.32 through the quarter and the rupee ~94.8-95.4, so reported USD revenue lands ~0.2-0.3% below cc (JM already models USD -0.6% vs cc -0.5%) and the weaker rupee is a ~10-20bp margin tailwind that is part of the +40bp consensus. Nets to roughly zero against the published bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No evidence this name has traded on a cross-currency gap; the Q1 FY27 reported/cc gap (-1.4% vs -1.2%) drew no comment.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside the brokers' USD-vs-cc modelling, which is why it is sized at zero; filed so the panel sees the FX arithmetic was checked.
findings.independence: Guide FX assumptions from the company release (wipro.com press-release-q1fy27.pdf, 2026-07-16); USD/INR 94.84 on 2026-09-08 https://dollarrupee.in/. The quarter averages were not found as a published series; the levels are daily snapshots.

findings.finding: ADR-specific positioning: 102.8M ADS short with 14.2 days to cover, a sell-side of 4 Sell / 0 Buy with a $1.70 consensus target below the $1.80 spot, the ADR 41.5% off its 52-week high and 11% off the 09-24 low of $1.645, and a line that moved -16.9% in one session on a JPMorgan downgrade with no company news (2026-07-02) while the NSE line rose 2.25% the same day. The release comes after the NSE close (~06:00 ET) with the call at 09:30 ET, so the ADR is the only line trading the result on 10-15 and the whole first reaction lands in this window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ADR's reactions are larger than the NSE line's in both directions: -16.9% on a downgrade (07-02) vs NSE +2.25%; ADR -2.2% on the 04-16 print. Realised vol 37.5% annualised.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up (+7.2% in 5 sessions) says some of the asymmetry is already bought. What is not: the short is 14 days of ADR volume, and a print that merely matches the -2% to 0% guide expectation against a Strong Sell consensus has nobody positioned for it on this line. If it were priced the ADR would not sit below the only published target with a 14-day cover.
findings.independence: Short interest https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/WIT/short-interest (2026-09-30 settlement, published 2026-10-09); ratings and 52-week low https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-wipro-nyse-wit-sets-new-12-month-low-heres-why-2026-09-24/; release timing https://www.uniindia.com/business-wire-india/wipro-limited-to-announce-results-for-the-second-quarter-ended-september-30-2026-on-october-15-2026/205949 (2026-10-07). Shares one fact (the run-up) with finding 1's why_not_priced; sized apart because this one is about the ADR line's own mechanics, not the sector read.

baseline_tension: No skew is readable and the history is void; what I found leans with the 5-day run-up (sector prints bought, low sell-side bar) and against nothing in the baseline, which is why the lean is small: the run-up has already bought part of the peer read.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 / rule 5: the peer read is a proxy and this ADR has sold most of its own prints, so finding 1 shrank from +1.0 to +0.8 and p_up moved from 55 to 53 (not toward the proxy's optimism).
Rule 9: the Meta cut was re-sized net of the rest of the company (0.24% of revenue against 13 large deals and a full Mindsprint quarter), -0.5 to -0.4.
Rule 3: the AlphaNet item's own caveat (JM's attribution is one line and may not be in its Q2 number) reached the size, -0.4 to -0.3.
Rule 7: positioning finding trimmed +0.6 to +0.5 because the run-up already carries part of it; the short is 1.05% of float, crowded only by days-to-cover.
The 'reaction history built from the wrong events' rule confirmed the base rate was rebuilt from confirmed ADR print reactions; abs_move_pct 4.5 unchanged.
Nothing was dropped; the FX finding stays at 0.0 as filed.
